reason: Driven in chromium on fresh loads with nothing clicked, document.activeElement === BODY, and the finding's measurements reproduce exactly. .scroll (lately.html:171) is height:100vh; overflow-y:auto with tabIndex -1 and no tabindex attribute, inside .canvas overflow:hidden (:170) and .app min-height:100% (:153) under html, body { height: 100% } (:116). Space, PageDown, ArrowDown and End each left .scroll.scrollTop at 0 on full@1440 (664px of hidden overflow), full@390 (1820px), partial@1440 (759px) and loading@390 (1021px); the wheel moved 400px in the same frames, and after a single Tab onto the tab strip PageDown moved 664px at 1440 and 738px at 390. Every cited line number and selector is correct against the source. I extended the sweep: the same dead keys reproduce on quiet and first-run at 390/768/1280/1440 too, so it is every scrollable state at every width, not a subset. One imprecision that does not change the verdict: the sentence 'the document itself has zero scrollable overflow' is true for full, partial, quiet and first-run but not for loading@390, where the document carries 779px of its own overflow and the keys scroll the whole shell while the reading content still sits at 0 - which is worse, not better. Nothing in interaction-check.mjs asserts keyboard scrolling; its only .scroll reference (:1196) drives the container programmatically, so the gate has never touched this. Nothing in lessons.md covers the class. It is not on the closed or refuted lists. The fix is right as written and I measured it: injecting exactly the proposed declarations (body min-height, .app min-height:100vh, sticky 100vh align-self:flex-start rail, .canvas overflow dropped, .scroll reduced to overflow-x:clip) makes PageDown from BODY move the document on the first press in all 20 scrollable state/viewport combinations and End reaches the true bottom every time; documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth stayed 0 in all 28 combinations before and after scrolling; the rail stayed pinned at top 0 (sub-pixel -0.47 to 0) at 768 and above and is display:none below 561 (:531), so the sticky rule is inert exactly where the rail is. overflow-x:clip is the correct choice over hidden: hidden on one axis forces the other to auto and would have reinstated the same trap, clip does not. The tooltip claim also holds - the tip is a body-level position:fixed element (:389, :543) and its listener is window/capture (:1116), so I ran the gate's own touch-pin-then-scroll procedure at 390 both ways and got identical results (pinned, drift 8px) whether the 260px came from .scroll.scrollBy or window.scrollBy. Severity: defect is correct and I would not raise it. The surface does render everything it claims and a keyboard-only reader who presses Tab first - the natural first keyboard act - gets a working PageDown, so it is not blocking and it asserts nothing untrue. But it sits at the top of the class: the primary reading gesture on a reading instrument is dead on arrival at every width, and on the phone that leaves 1820 of 2664px, including the whole 'What this can't tell you' movement, behind a fold the gesture will not cross.
sharpenedFix: Land the fix exactly as proposed - the declarations and line numbers are right and measure correct. Add two things with it, both in interaction-check.mjs. First, repoint line 1196: `document.querySelector('.scroll').scrollBy(0, 260)` becomes a silent no-op once .scroll stops being a scroll container, which would leave the stale-tip-strands-on-scroll assertion passing vacuously forever; change it to `window.scrollBy(0, 260)`. Second, add the assertion this finding exists for, so the trap cannot return: on a fresh load with document.activeElement === BODY, press PageDown and assert document.scrollingElement.scrollTop > 0 for every state with overflow at 390/768/1280/1440.
breaks: Little, but three things must be re-measured. (1) interaction-check.mjs:1196 drives .scroll.scrollBy directly; after the fix that call moves nothing and the stale-tip assertion goes vacuous - repoint it at window before trusting the gate green. (2) The 'no sideways scroll' assertion (:89-91) has until now been guaranteed by .canvas overflow:hidden masking anything wide; after the fix only .scroll's overflow-x:clip clips it, so re-run that assertion across all seven states and all four widths - I measured 0px in all 28, but it is now load-bearing where it was previously masked. (3) The rail becomes sticky rather than stretched, so its right hairline is now painted by a 100vh box that is repositioned on every scroll frame rather than a full-height one; re-shoot the 768 and 1280 frames scrolled to the bottom and check the hairline still runs edge to edge and does not seam against the canvas. Also re-run audit.mjs: the fix changes no colour, weight, size or gap, but the shots it reads are regenerated from a page whose scroll box changed, and scroll-position-dependent captures should be re-taken from the top. Nothing in the script needs editing - confirmed by driving, not only by reading.
